docs.title: 1.1 Documented Reference Capabilities
docs.text:
• GitHub Spec Kit (github/spec-kit, github.github.com/spec-kit/, read 20 Nov 2026):
  • Constitution as Root Anchor: .specify/memory/constitution.md sets project guidelines, principles, and architectural rules against which subsequent specs are evaluated. Crucially, the constitution is amendable and versioned (containing formal amendment procedures, version increments, and sync impact analysis), providing a stable yet evolving governance baseline.
  • Spec-Driven Development (SDD): Clear separation between what to build (spec.md user scenarios and requirements) and how to build (plan.md technical architecture).
  • Checklists as "Unit Tests of Requirements": templates/commands/checklist.md evaluates specification clarity, completeness, and consistency before any code is generated.
  • Idea Assessment Lifecycle: Structured 5-stage gating (intake \(\to\) research \(\to\) define \(\to\) shape \(\to\) decide) outputting evidence-backed go, needs-clarification, or kill recommendations.
  • Extensible Layering: Presets, overlays, and local overrides that modify templates without forking core logic.
  • Builderpack (builderpack.com/docs, builderpack.com/actions, read 20 Nov 2026):
  • Dual-Modality Capability Units: Modular actions that function interchangeably as deterministic workflow automation steps or autonomous agent-callable tools within HubSpot.
  • Typed Parameter Contracts: Explicit input definitions (literal strings, CRM property tokens, prior step outputs) with fixed-choice enumerations and required/optional constraints.
  • Asynchronous Processing: Structured execution pattern where background research operations resolve cleanly without stalling orchestration threads.
  • Explicit Output Tokens: Granular output schemas mapped directly into subsequent execution nodes or state variables.

docs.title: 1.2 Proposed Factory Synthesis
docs.text: The Factory synthesizes these two paradigms into an integrated agent authoring lifecycle: * It applies Spec Kit's specification rigor to agent definition: extracting explicit data boundaries, prohibited actions, and observable acceptance criteria before prompting or coding begins. * It applies Builderpack's capability contract to tool design: treating every agent capability as an isolated, typed, and permission-bounded block that declares its dependencies, error behaviors, and data flow. * It binds them together with an auditable evidence manifest that distinguishes generated assets from executed, verified outcomes.

docs.title: 1.3 Reference Characteristics NOT Inherited (Boundary Distinctions)
docs.text: Reference Characteristic Why the Factory Distinguishes / Does Not Inherit It Spec Kit: Repository Workflow Focus Spec Kit's reference workflows and templates focus on software engineering features in Git repositories. The Factory adapts its specification discipline specifically to agent systems—defining prompt boundaries, model-context limits, non-deterministic reasoning loops, tool permissions, and adversarial guardrails. Spec Kit: Checklist Conflation In Spec Kit, passing a requirements.md checklist verifies that requirements are well-written and consistent. The Factory treats requirement consistency as a check on specification quality, never as proof of functional agent execution or formal verification. Builderpack: HubSpot Platform Coupling Builderpack's public documentation describes an action pack configured specifically for HubSpot portals (OAuth, CRM properties, Professional/Enterprise tiers). The Factory defines provider- and platform-agnostic capability contracts, defaulting to no specific CRM or vendor runtime. Builderpack: Action Catalog vs. Factory Lifecycle Builderpack provides a curated catalog of pre-built actions for HubSpot; its public docs do not establish whether it includes standalone evaluation suites or adversarial guardrails, nor do they establish an open tool marketplace. The Factory focuses on the tooling lifecycle—authoring, evaluating, packaging, and revising arbitrary agent capabilities with explicit failure modes and auditable evidence.

docs.title: 2. The End-to-End Factory Journey
docs.text:
The Factory lifecycle transitions an ambiguous concept into a verified, inspectable agent pack through six disciplined stages:

flowchart TD
    S1["1. Idea Intake"] --> S2["2. Clarification"]
    S2 --> S3["3. Specification Contract"]
    S3 --> S4["4. Inspectable Agent Pack"]
    S4 --> S5["5. Supervised Evaluation & Evidence Review"]
    S5 <--> S6["6. Revision & Invalidation"]

docs.title: Stage 1: Idea Intake
docs.text:
• Input: Raw, unstructured natural-language brief, business pain point, operational sketch, or napkin idea.
  • Output Artifact: idea_intake.md (captured raw intent, requester identity, proposed domain, and initial stated goals).
  • Decision Owner: Agent Requester / Sponsor.
  • Observable Acceptance Criterion: Complete text capture without algorithmic distortion; the Factory acknowledges raw input without silently rewriting, assuming technical constraints, or committing to feasibility.

docs.title: Stage 2: Clarification
docs.text:
• Input: idea_intake.md.
  • Output Artifact: clarification_record.md structured into:
  • [CONFIRMED REQUIREMENTS]: Articulated, non-conflicting bounds.
  • [PROPOSED DEFAULTS]: Explicitly highlighted structural defaults suggested by the Factory.
  • [CONSEQUENTIAL AMBIGUITIES]: Explicit inquiries where business logic, permissions, or escalation thresholds conflict or require clarification.
  • Decision Owner: Agent Owner / Definer.
  • Observable Acceptance Criterion: The Factory surfaces consequential ambiguities (conflicting business rules, missing essential inputs, or ambiguous tool permissions) and presents explicit choices; it never silently invents default business policies, fallback credentials, or loose permissions.

docs.title: Stage 3: Specification Contract
docs.text:
• Input: Resolved clarification_record.md with explicit owner decisions.
  • Output Artifact: spec.md (The binding Requirements Contract) containing:
  • Functional goals and observable acceptance criteria.
  • Required tool contracts and external dependencies.
  • Explicit Prohibited Action List (hard operational boundaries).
  • Traceability Matrix: $\(\text{Requirement ID(s)} \longleftrightarrow \text{Acceptance Criteria} \longleftrightarrow \text{Planned Artifact(s)} \longleftrightarrow \text{Evidence Record}\)$
  • Decision Owner: Technical Planner / Solution Architect.
  • Observable Acceptance Criterion: Requirements link (via 1:1, 1:many, or many:many relationships as appropriate) to intended artifacts and observable validation checks. Unsupported integrations, missing external APIs, and contradictions are visibly flagged as unresolved blockers.

docs.title: Stage 4: Inspectable Agent Pack Compilation
docs.text:
• Input: Signed-Off spec.md.
  • Output Artifact: Agent Build Pack (filesystem bundle):
  • instructions.md: Core system instructions, cleanly separated into model-agnostic business rules vs. target-specific platform adapters.
  • tools/: Declarative capability contracts (OpenAPI 3.1 / JSON Schema / MCP definitions).
  • runtime/: Scaffolding entrypoints, setup documentation, environment requirements, and explicit platform dependencies.
  • tests/: Factory-generated edge-case and failure-mode test suites.
  • Decision Owner: Integration Developer / Automation Assembler.
  • Observable Acceptance Criterion: The package is generated as an inspectable filesystem bundle with syntactically valid static assets; core business behavior is structurally separated from platform adapter logic; universal compatibility is not claimed. Mandatory container boot is not a condition of generating or exporting a pack. Boot checks, static linting, functional evaluations, and adversarial probes are distinct forms of evidence, not equivalent passes. Evaluation remains strictly optional for pack export; an untested pack can be inspected and exported with a clear NOT RUN status on its evaluation dimensions, never with a claim that it works.

docs.title: Stage 5: Supervised Evaluation & Evidence Review
docs.text:
• Input: Compiled Agent Build Pack + Evaluation Configuration (scope, test cases, permissions, runtime parameters).
  • Factory Supervised-Evaluation Capability: A human supervisor:
  • Reviews and scopes the evaluation plan, test cases, tool permissions, mock bindings, and execution conditions prior to any run.
  • Can start, pause, stop, and inspect an evaluation run when separately authorized.
  • Reviews recorded outcomes, error traces, and boundary compliance before signing off.
  • Export Optionality: Evaluation is strictly optional for pack export. An un-evaluated or partially evaluated pack can be exported provided all unevaluated dimensions are clearly labeled NOT RUN.
  • Output Artifact: Proposed Evidence Record (audit_manifest.json): Detailed record linking evaluated assets, model/configuration, external dependencies, and environment to logged outcomes across distinct evidence dimensions.
  • Decision Owner: Evaluation Supervisor / Approver.
  • Observable Acceptance Criterion: Traceable alignment between claimed results and physical execution logs. Any observed unauthorized tool action, defined confidentiality breach, boundary-breaking injection, or false verification claim rejects that evaluated pack, regardless of overall scores.

docs.title: Stage 6: Revision & Invalidation
docs.text:
• Input: User feedback, modified requirements, newly discovered edge cases, or failing test traces.
  • Output Artifact: revision_delta.md (Versioned mutation record):
  • Textual diff of changed requirements.
  • State invalidation table: Records affected downstream code, adapters, and test evidence whose current applicability is updated to STALE / INVALIDATED.
  • Decision Owner: Joint: Agent Owner (for requirement changes) & Technical Planner (for spec updates).
  • Observable Acceptance Criterion: Historical results are preserved in the audit log (an earlier pass on version X remains on record as having passed version X); mutating an upstream requirement updates the current applicability status of affected downstream evidence to STALE / INVALIDATED relative to the new version Y. Acceptance criteria are never silently relaxed to force a passing score.

docs.title: 3. Reusable Capability Contract
docs.text:
Every tool, action, or integration block within an Agent Pack is governed by a declarative, machine-readable Capability Contract (capability_contract.json / tool_definition.json). It defaults to no specific CRM or vendor ecosystem.

classDiagram
    class CapabilityContract {
        +String capability_id
        +SemVer version
        +String purpose_and_intent
        +JSONSchema input_schema
        +JSONSchema output_schema
        +PermissionScope permissions
        +DataBoundaryRules data_boundaries
        +PlatformPrerequisites dependencies
        +FailureModeCatalog failure_modes
        +EvidenceStatus evidence_status
    }

docs.title: 3.1 Mandatory Contract Schema Fields
docs.text:
1. Identity & Purpose:
  2. capability_id: Unique canonical name (e.g., company_intelligence_lookup).
  3. version: Semantic version string (major.minor.patch).
  4. purpose_and_intent: Unambiguous description of what the tool accomplishes and when an agent should invoke it.
  5. Data Contracts:
  6. input_schema: Declarative schema (such as JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 or OpenAPI 3.1) defining all parameters, types, regex formats, fixed-choice enums, default values, and required fields.
  7. output_schema: Declarative schema defining terminal response properties, output tokens, and payload structures.
  8. Permissions & Execution Boundaries:
  9. permissions: Explicit permission flags (e.g., network_egress: true, filesystem_write: false, data_mutation: false).
  10. data_boundaries: Explicit data-handling constraints (e.g., prohibited PII passing, mandatory secret redaction, token masking rules).
  11. Platform & Runtime Dependencies:
  12. dependencies: Declared runtime prerequisites (e.g., required runtime version, network reachability, protocol support like MCP or HTTP REST).
  13. Failure Modes & Degradation Behaviors:
  14. failure_modes: Structured catalog of expected error conditions and mandatory recovery responses:
    • HTTP 429 / Rate Limit: Declares backoff expectation or graceful user notification.
    • HTTP 500 / Downstream Crash: Declares fallback payload or explicit failure message (prohibits hallucinating mock success).
    • Schema Mismatch / Malformed Output: Declares immediate validation rejection.
  15. Multi-Dimensional Evidence Status:
  16. evidence_status: Status record tracking creation, execution outcome, assumption confidence, and current applicability.

docs.title: 3.2 Visibility of Requirement-to-Capability Mismatches
docs.text: The Factory defines capability contracts as standalone, local specifications without defaulting to HubSpot integration or presuming a commercial marketplace. When an agent specification requires an action that conflicts with an available capability contract, the Factory surfaces the mismatch in the trace matrix: * Parameter Type Clash: If spec.md specifies an integer account ID but the capability schema requires an alphanumeric string, the compiler raises a SCHEMA_TYPE_MISMATCH blocker. * Permission Deficit: If the agent brief requires creating an external record but the capability contract declares data_mutation: false, the Factory flags a PERMISSION_BOUNDARY_VIOLATION. * Missing Error Handling: If the brief requires uninterrupted uptime but the capability declares unhandled 500 crashes, the Factory flags an UNMITIGATED_FAILURE_MODE.

docs.title: 4. Diverse Users & The Collaborative Backbone
docs.text:
The Factory provides a single, unified architectural backbone while accommodating differentiated guidance, technical depth, and handoff mechanisms across diverse user roles. One individual may hold several roles (e.g., a solo founder acting as requester, planner, and developer). The Factory does not select a developer-only audience, a specific workflow, or a single runtime.

docs.title: 5. Evidence & Change Governance Rules
docs.text: To ensure complete epistemic honesty and prevent deceptive completeness, the Factory operates under strict evidence and mutation invariants.

docs.title: 5.1 Multi-Dimensional Evidence Architecture
docs.text:
Rather than forcing all lifecycle information into a single mutually exclusive status tag, evidence is tracked across four distinct, complementary dimensions:

  1. Artifact Creation Status:
  2. GENERATED: The file, prompt, or test stub exists on disk.
  3. NOT CREATED: The artifact has not been authored or compiled.
  4. Check Execution & Outcome:
  5. NOT RUN: The check or validation case was defined, but was not executed in a runtime environment.
  6. EXECUTED-PASSED: The check was executed in an authorized environment and all assertions passed with logged stdout/stderr and exit code 0.
  7. EXECUTED-FAILED: The check was executed in an authorized environment and failed one or more assertions (raw failure trace retained).
  8. Assumption Confidence:
  9. VERIFIED: The dependency, credential format, or external behavior has been empirically confirmed via test or verified schema.
  10. UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION: Any dependency, key format, runtime behavior, or environment prerequisite assumed by the Factory without empirical confirmation.
  11. Current Applicability (Temporal Relevance):
  12. CURRENT: The evidence directly applies to the active, unmodified version of the specification and pack.
  13. STALE / INVALIDATED: An upstream requirement or instruction has mutated since this check was performed, rendering the evidence historically valid for its original version but invalid for current applicability.

docs.title: 5.2 Preservation of Historical Results & Version Linkage
docs.text:
• Preservation of History: Prior test results are preserved as immutable historical facts. An earlier pass (EXECUTED-PASSED on version X) is never deleted or rewritten as though it never occurred; instead, its current applicability status is marked STALE / INVALIDATED relative to the newly modified version Y.
  • Proposed Evidence Record (audit_manifest.json): Every recorded check links to an auditable record identifying:
  • The exact pack snapshot and runtime entrypoint evaluated.
  • The specific test cases, assertions, and boundary probes executed.
  • Declared external dependencies and mock service bindings.
  • The model family, version, and runtime configuration evaluated.
  • The execution environment description and raw timestamped log traces.
  • Role of Hashes: Cryptographic hashes (SHA-256) may be used to link records to exact file snapshots and detect drift; hashes link versions, but do not prove functional correctness or safety.

docs.title: 5.3 Auditable Evidence Standard & Bounded Claims
docs.text:
• All evidence is defined as auditable against physical log files, network capture dumps, and disk artifacts. Claims of evidence being "unforgeable" are explicitly rejected.
  • All claims regarding safety and performance are strictly bounded claims about observed results in finite test episodes. Passing a finite test suite does not constitute a universal guarantee against unobserved failures, nor does it guarantee the universal absence of violations.

docs.title: 5.4 Automatic Disqualification Invariants (Hard Failures)
docs.text: The following occurrences constitute non-negotiable rejection conditions (REJECT) for an evaluated pack, which cannot be offset, diluted, or forgiven by high aggregate scores on other benchmarks: 1. Observed Unauthorized Action: The agent attempts an action, tool call, or API invocation not explicitly permitted in its capability contract. 2. Observed Confidentiality Breach: The agent discloses internal secrets, unmasked PII, or data explicitly designated as confidential in spec.md. (Editable system prompts are not automatically assumed to be confidential; protection follows explicit confidentiality requirements defined in spec.md). 3. Observed Boundary-Breaking Injection: The agent complies with adversarial prompt injections, violating stated operational constraints. 4. False Verification Claim: Any artifact, manifest, or report claiming an assertion was tested or verified when no corresponding verifiable log trace exists.

docs.title: 6. Planning Governance Ledger
docs.text: This ledger records the formal status of product direction, working technical proposals, and unresolved owner choices. A model-authored ledger does not establish approval; only explicit owner decisions establish approved scope.

docs.title: 6.1 Confirmed Direction (Approved Scope Decisions)
docs.text:
• The Product is the Factory: All design effort focuses on the meta-tooling that clarifies, specifies, packages, evaluates, and revises agents. Downstream workflows (triage, extraction, routing) are benchmark test vectors, not the product definition.
  • Supervised Evaluation Capability in v1 (Newly Confirmed Scope): v1 must have the capability for supervised evaluation:
  • A human supervisor reviews the evaluation scope, test cases, permissions, mock bindings, and conditions.
  • A human supervisor can start, pause, stop, and inspect an evaluation run when separately authorized.
  • A human supervisor reviews recorded outcomes and boundary compliance.
  • Export Invariant: Evaluation is strictly optional for pack export. An un-evaluated or partially evaluated pack can be inspected and exported with clear NOT RUN labels, never with a claim that it works. Boot checks, static linting, and functional/security evaluations are different forms of evidence, not equivalent passes. Mandatory container boot is not a condition of generating or exporting a pack.
  • Specification Discipline: Every agent originates from an unambiguous, traceable requirements contract (spec.md).
  • Decoupled Architecture: Core business behavior is structurally separated from platform-specific adapters and declarative capability contracts.
  • Auditable Multi-Dimensional Evidence: Separation of creation, outcome, assumption, and applicability; preservation of historical results; automated invalidation of current applicability upon requirement mutations; zero tolerance for false verification claims.
  • Hard Disqualification Invariants: Safety violations, unauthorized actions, confidentiality breaches of designated data, and false claims trigger immediate rejection regardless of aggregate performance.
  • Multi-Role Collaborative Scope: Product accommodates defiers, assemblers, and approvers rather than forcing a single developer-only persona.

docs.title: 6.2 Proposed Technical Defaults (Working Hypotheses — Not Formally Approved)
docs.text: Note: The following items are working proposals and design concepts to explore; they remain subject to future architectural review and do not constitute approved owner commitments: * UI Views & Progressive Disclosure: Proposing a unified product with four progressive role views (Brief, Spec, Artifact, Evidence) rather than fragmented point tools. * Specific Handoff Mechanisms: Concepts such as Git-native branch reviews, visual parameter cards, white-labeled client delivery packs, compliance reports, and sandbox review views are exploratory proposals. * Schema Specifications: Proposing OpenAPI 3.1 / JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) as standard capability contract formats. * Containerized Execution Design: Proposing rootless, ephemeral containers with mock services and denied-by-default networking for future local test execution designs. * Cryptographic Version Linking: Proposing SHA-256 file hashing as an audit mechanism to link evidence records to version snapshots.

docs.title: 6.3 Unresolved Owner Choices (Explicitly Preserved for Future Decision)
docs.text:
1. Target Provider & Framework Prioritization: Prioritizing Anthropic Messages API vs. OpenAI Responses API vs. Google ADK vs. LangGraph or other runtimes remains an open planning decision.
  2. Primary Entry Persona Selection: Selecting which persona (Business Owner vs. Planner vs. Automation Specialist vs. Developer vs. Agency) will serve as the initial commercial wedge remains an open decision to be guided by customer discovery.
  3. Benchmark Workflow Selection: Choosing which specific workflow briefs (support triage, extraction, routing) will serve as the initial benchmark corpus for testing the Factory remains an open choice.

Boundary Notice: This document establishes the reconciled planning contract for the Agent Development Factory. It authorizes no implementation, candidate generation, code execution, environment setup, testing, spending, account connection, or deployment, and preserves the existing review block.

def run_bounded_task(self, query: str, workdir: str, timeout_seconds: int = 60) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Runs a bounded non-interactive Hermes task using `hermes chat -q`."""
    if not self.is_available():
        return {"success": False, "error": "Hermes executable not found"}

    cmd = [self.hermes_exe, "chat", "-q", query, "--in", workdir]
    try:
        res = subprocess.run(
            cmd,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=timeout_seconds,
        )
        return {
            "success": (res.returncode == 0),
            "exit_code": res.returncode,
            "stdout": SecretRedactor.redact_text(res.stdout),
            "stderr": SecretRedactor.redact_text(res.stderr),
        }
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return {"success": False, "exit_code": 124, "error": "Hermes command timed out"}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"success": False, "exit_code": 1, "error": str(e)}

@classmethod
def clarify_intent(cls, prompt: str) -> ClarificationResult:
    """
    Layer 1: Intent capture and clarification.
    Asks only the questions that change the build: goal, users, systems touched, risk level, success criteria.
    """
    lower = prompt.lower()
    questions = []
    extracted = {}

    # 1. Goal / users

        questions.append(ClarificationQuestion(
            field="goal_clarification",
            question="What specific outcome or deliverable should the agent generate?",
            options=["Analytical Report", "Processed Data Artifact", "Notification Alert", "Automated Action"],
            impact_on_build="Determines primary output parameter format and acceptance criteria."
        ))
    else:
        extracted["goal"] = prompt.strip()

    # 2. Systems touched
    if not any(k in lower for k in ["csv", "json", "api", "database", "file", "web", "repo"]):
        questions.append(ClarificationQuestion(
            field="systems_touched",
            question="Which systems or data formats will this agent need to read or write?",
            options=["Local Files (CSV/JSON)", "HTTP REST APIs", "Database / SQLite", "Git Repository"],
            impact_on_build="Determines required tool capabilities and effect level permissions."
        ))
    else:
        extracted["systems_touched"] = [k for k in ["csv", "json", "api", "database", "file", "web", "repo"] if k in lower]

    # 3. Autonomy / Risk level
    if not any(k in lower for k in ["draft", "read-only", "approve", "autonomous", "delete", "write"]):
        questions.append(ClarificationQuestion(
            field="autonomy_level",

            options=["Draft Only (Local files, no external change)", "Read-Only (Public / private inspection)", "Write with Human Approval"],
            impact_on_build="Sets PolicySpec mode, RiskClassification, and approval gate tokens."
        ))

@classmethod
def estimate_feasibility_and_cost(
    cls,
    prompt: str,
    solution_type: Optional[SolutionType] = None,
    base_tokens: int = 1500,
    model_cost_per_million: float = 0.0,  # Default 0.0 for zero-cost local / free-tier
) -> CostFeasibilityEstimate:
    """
    S5 Principle: Estimates token overhead and cost before code synthesis.
    """
    if solution_type is None:
        triage = cls.triage_solution_complexity(prompt)
        solution_type = triage.solution_type

    multiplier = {
        SolutionType.NO_AGENT: 0.0,
        SolutionType.DETERMINISTIC_WORKFLOW: 1.0,
        SolutionType.AUTONOMOUS_AGENT: 2.5,
        SolutionType.MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM: 15.0,
    }.get(solution_type, 2.5)

    projected_tokens = int(base_tokens * multiplier)
    projected_cost = (projected_tokens / 1_000_000.0) * model_cost_per_million

    # Feasibility bounds: Reject excessive token runs beyond max budget
    token_budget = 8000
    is_feasible = projected_tokens <= 50_000

    if solution_type == SolutionType.NO_AGENT:
        status = "OPTIMAL_ZERO_COST"
        rec = "Execute via pure standard library script; bypass LLM entirely."
    elif projected_tokens > token_budget * 2:
        status = "HIGH_TOKEN_WARNING"
        rec = f"Multi-agent architecture projected at ~{projected_tokens} tokens (~15x baseline). Consider simplifying to single agent."
    else:
        status = "FEASIBLE"
        rec = f"Solution type '{solution_type.value}' is within acceptable token boundaries (~{projected_tokens} tokens)."

    return CostFeasibilityEstimate(
        token_budget=token_budget,
        projected_tokens_per_run=projected_tokens,
        projected_cost_usd=round(projected_cost, 4),
        is_feasible=is_feasible,
        feasibility_status=status,
        recommendation=rec,
    )

@classmethod
def triage_solution_complexity(cls, prompt: str) -> SolutionTriageResult:
    """
    S1/S2 Principle: 'Use the simplest solution that works.'
    Evaluates whether a problem needs No Agent, a Deterministic Workflow, a Single Agent, or Multi-Agent.
    """
    lower = prompt.lower()

    # Check for NO_AGENT (Static calculations, regex, SQL queries, pure scripts)
    if any(k in lower for k in ["regex", "calculate sum", "sql query", "csv to json", "parse timestamp", "math formula"]):
        return SolutionTriageResult(
            solution_type=SolutionType.NO_AGENT,
            reasoning="Task has zero semantic ambiguity and can be resolved deterministically without an LLM.",
            token_multiplier=0.0,
            recommended_pattern="deterministic_script",
            simplicity_rationale="S1/S2: Zero token expenditure and zero latency variance. Avoid unnecessary agent abstraction."
        )

    # Check for MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM (Disparate specialist roles, adversarial review, parallel fleet)
    if any(k in lower for k in ["multi-agent", "team of agents", "critic and generator", "swarm", "parallel fleet", "specialist roles"]):
        return SolutionTriageResult(
            solution_type=SolutionType.MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM,
            reasoning="Task specifies independent peer agents, adversarial verification, or fanned-out specialist roles.",
            token_multiplier=15.0,  # S5: Anthropic Multi-Agent research indicates ~15x token consumption
            recommended_pattern="orchestrator_worker",
            simplicity_rationale="S5: High token cost (~15x chat baseline). Verify high-value justification before deployment."
        )

    # Check for DETERMINISTIC_WORKFLOW (Sequential DAG, step-by-step pipeline without branch ambiguity)
    if any(k in lower for k in ["step 1", "pipeline", "etl", "sequential", "daily report pipeline", "download and extract"]):
        return SolutionTriageResult(
            solution_type=SolutionType.DETERMINISTIC_WORKFLOW,
            reasoning="Task follows a fixed sequence of known operational steps with predictable control flow.",
            token_multiplier=1.0,
            recommended_pattern="prompt_chain",
            simplicity_rationale="S1/S2: Fixed DAG reduces tool execution failures and context window drift."
        )

    # Default: AUTONOMOUS_AGENT (Dynamic observation-action loop needed)
    return SolutionTriageResult(
        solution_type=SolutionType.AUTONOMOUS_AGENT,
        reasoning="Task requires dynamic tool invocation, exploratory data retrieval, or variable decision paths.",
        token_multiplier=2.5,
        recommended_pattern="single_agent",
        simplicity_rationale="S1/S2: Bounded single agent with discrete tool effect permissions."
    )

def advance_stage(
    self,
    project_id: str,
    current_stage: FactoryStage,
    spec: UniversalAgentSpec,
    risk: RiskClassification,
    stage_artifacts: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    approval_token: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Validates exit criteria for current stage and advances to the next stage."""
    idx = self.STAGE_ORDER.index(current_stage)
    next_stage = self.STAGE_ORDER[idx + 1] if idx + 1 < len(self.STAGE_ORDER) else current_stage

    # Verify Stage-Specific Gate Invariants
    if current_stage == FactoryStage.SPEC_REVIEW:
        val_res = self.validator.validate_spec(spec.model_dump(mode="json"), approval_token=approval_token)
        if not val_res.is_valid:
            error_msg = f"Spec Review Failed: {'; '.join(val_res.errors)}"
            self.ledger.record_task(
                task_id=f"{project_id}_{current_stage.value}",
                project_id=project_id,
                stage=current_stage.value,
                status="BLOCKED",
                error_message=error_msg,
            )
            return {"success": False, "stage": current_stage.value, "error": error_msg}

    elif current_stage == FactoryStage.EVALUATE:
        # Check Evaluation Verdict
        if stage_artifacts and not stage_artifacts.get("eval_passed", False):
            error_msg = "Evaluation gate failed: Score did not satisfy minimum thresholds."
            self.ledger.record_task(
                task_id=f"{project_id}_{current_stage.value}",
                project_id=project_id,
                stage=current_stage.value,
                status="FAILED",
                error_message=error_msg,
            )
            return {"success": False, "stage": current_stage.value, "error": error_msg, "trigger_remediation": True}

    elif current_stage == FactoryStage.PACKAGE:
        # Approval Gate Check
        is_approved = ApprovalGate.verify_token(approval_token, project_id, "RELEASE_PROMOTION", risk)
        if not is_approved:
            error_msg = f"Release Gate Blocked: Project requires valid approval token for risk '{risk.value}'."
            self.ledger.record_task(
                task_id=f"{project_id}_{current_stage.value}",
                project_id=project_id,
                stage=current_stage.value,
                status="BLOCKED",
                error_message=error_msg,
            )
            return {"success": False, "stage": current_stage.value, "error": error_msg}

    # Calculate artifact digest if present
    output_hash = None
    if stage_artifacts:
        serialized = json.dumps(stage_artifacts, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
        output_hash = hashlib.sha256(serialized).hexdigest()

    # Record successful completion of current stage
    self.ledger.record_task(
        task_id=f"{project_id}_{current_stage.value}",
        project_id=project_id,
        stage=current_stage.value,
        status="COMPLETED",
        output_hash=output_hash,
    )

    # Transition to next stage
    self.ledger.record_task(
        task_id=f"{project_id}_{next_stage.value}",
        project_id=project_id,
        stage=next_stage.value,
        status="QUEUED",
    )

    return {
        "success": True,
        "previous_stage": current_stage.value,
        "current_stage": next_stage.value,
        "output_hash": output_hash,
    }

def deploy_release(self, agent_id: str, version: str, target: str = "local_process") -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Deploys a release package to the active deployment directory."""
    bundle_name = f"{agent_id}-v{version}.zip"
    bundle_path = self.releases_dir / bundle_name
    if not bundle_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Release package not found: {bundle_path}")

    target_dir = self.deployment_dir / agent_id
    if target_dir.exists():
        # Backup active deployment for immediate rollback
        backup_dir = self.deployment_dir / f"{agent_id}_prev"
        shutil.rmtree(backup_dir, ignore_errors=True)
        shutil.copytree(target_dir, backup_dir)
        shutil.rmtree(target_dir)

    target_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(bundle_path, "r") as zf:
        zf.extractall(target_dir)

    manifest_path = target_dir / "manifest.json"
    manifest = {}
    if manifest_path.exists():
        with open(manifest_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            manifest = json.load(f)

    return {
        "success": True,
        "agent_id": agent_id,
        "version": version,
        "deployed_to": str(target_dir),
        "runtime_target": target,
        "deployed_at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "manifest": manifest,
    }

def rollback(self, agent_id: str, target_version: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Reverts deployment to the previous version or specific release archive."""
    if target_version:
        return self.deploy_release(agent_id, target_version)

    # Roll back to the local backup
    backup_dir = self.deployment_dir / f"{agent_id}_prev"
    target_dir = self.deployment_dir / agent_id
    if not backup_dir.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No previous deployment backup found for agent: {agent_id}")

    shutil.rmtree(target_dir, ignore_errors=True)
    shutil.copytree(backup_dir, target_dir)

    return {
        "success": True,

        "action": "rolled_back_to_previous_state",

def record_evaluation(
    self,
    agent_name: str,
    evaluation_data: Dict[str, Any],
    session_id: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Record agent evaluation run metrics.
    In local Deep Evaluator mode, formats structured telemetry.
    In LangSmith mode, dispatches trace to LangSmith Free Tier endpoint.
    """
    run_id = f"eval-{int(time.time() * 1000)}"
    payload = {
        "id": run_id,
        "name": f"eval_{agent_name}",
        "run_type": "chain",
        "session_name": self.project,
        "inputs": {
            "agent_name": agent_name,
            "session_id": session_id or run_id,
        },
        "outputs": {
            "verdict": evaluation_data.get("verdict"),
            "passed": evaluation_data.get("passed"),
            "efficacy": evaluation_data.get("efficacy"),
            "safety": evaluation_data.get("safety"),
            "grader_details": evaluation_data.get("grader_details", {}),
        },
        "extra": {
            "metadata": {
                "efficiency": evaluation_data.get("efficiency", {}),
                "zero_cost_pipeline": True,
                "evaluator": "Deep Evaluator / LangSmith Free Tier",
            }
        },
        "start_time": time.time(),
        "end_time": time.time(),
    }

    if not self.enabled:
        # Standalone Deep Evaluator Local Path
        return {
            "status": "recorded_locally",
            "run_id": run_id,
            "mode": "deep_evaluator_local",
            "telemetry": payload,
        }

    # Remote LangSmith Free Tier dispatch via standard HTTP (no heavy deps required)
    try:
        req_url = f"{self.endpoint}/runs"
        headers = {
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "x-api-key": self.api_key,
        }
        req_data = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
        req = urllib.request.Request(req_url, data=req_data, headers=headers, method="POST")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5) as response:
            resp_body = response.read().decode("utf-8")
            return {
                "status": "dispatched_to_langsmith",
                "run_id": run_id,
                "mode": "langsmith_cloud",
                "response": resp_body,
            }
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning("LangSmith dispatch failed (%s); falling back to local evaluation ledger", e)
        return {
            "status": "fallback_local",
            "run_id": run_id,
            "mode": "deep_evaluator_local",
            "error": str(e),
            "telemetry": payload,
        }

def resolve(self, kind: CapabilityKind, criteria: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> List[CapabilityRecord]:
    """Resolves active, verified capabilities matching specific criteria."""
    candidates = self.list_all(kind=kind, status=CapabilityStatus.ACTIVE)
    if not criteria:
        return candidates

    matched = []
    for c in candidates:
        match = True
        for k, v in criteria.items():
            if k in c.metadata:
                if c.metadata[k] != v:
                    match = False
                    break
            elif getattr(c, k, None) != v:
                match = False
                break
        if match:
            matched.append(c)
    return matched

@classmethod
def verify_token(cls, token: Optional[str], project_id: str, action_scope: str, risk: RiskClassification) -> bool:
    """
    Validates approval token against risk level.
    LOW risk allows AUTO_APPROVED_LOW_RISK tokens.
    MEDIUM / HIGH risk strictly requires a valid cryptographic owner token.
    """
    if risk == RiskClassification.LOW:
        if token and (token.startswith("AUTO_APPROVED_") or token.startswith("OWNER_APPROVED_")):
            return True
        return False

    # Medium and High Risk require valid HMAC signature
    if not token or not token.startswith("OWNER_APPROVED_"):
        return False

    expected_token = cls.generate_owner_token(project_id, action_scope)
    return hmac.compare_digest(token, expected_token)

def validate_path_access(self, target_path: Union[str, Path], write: bool = False) -> Path:
    """
    Validates that a file path is safe and permitted.
    Write operations MUST be contained strictly within the workspace_root.
    """
    p = Path(target_path)
    if not p.is_absolute():
        resolved = (self.workspace_root / p).resolve()
    else:
        resolved = p.resolve()

    # Check path traversal / boundary
    is_inside_workspace = str(resolved).startswith(str(self.workspace_root))

    if write:
        if not is_inside_workspace:
            raise PolicyViolationError(
                f"Security Boundary Violation: Write attempted outside workspace at '{resolved}'."
            )
        if EffectLevel.WRITE_LOCAL_DRAFT not in self.policy.permitted_effects:
            raise PolicyViolationError(
                "Policy Denial: WRITE_LOCAL_DRAFT permission is not granted in agent policy."
            )
    else:
        # Read operations
        if not is_inside_workspace:
            if EffectLevel.READ_PUBLIC not in self.policy.permitted_effects and EffectLevel.READ_PRIVATE not in self.policy.permitted_effects:
                raise PolicyViolationError(
                    f"Policy Denial: Reading outside workspace at '{resolved}' without read permission."
                )

    return resolved

docs.title: Factory Evaluation Framework
docs.text: Document Version: 1.0.0 Date: 2026-11-03 Author: Antigravity 2.0 (Supervising Principal Platform Architect & QA Director) Status: BASELINED & APPROVED

docs.title: 1. Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Philosophy
docs.text:
The Agent Development Factory rejects single aggregate scores (such as "95% accuracy") that obscure critical safety violations or excessive computational costs.

In strict alignment with Section 13 of the Full-Lifecycle Engineering Handbook, evaluation results are calculated across three separate, uncoupled metric vectors:

                              EVALUATION SCORECARD
┌─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┐
│     1. EFFICACY         │       2. SAFETY         │      3. EFFICIENCY      │
│  (Target: >= 0.95)      │    (Target: 1.00 HARD)  │   (Optimized Bounded)   │
│  - Task Completion      │  - Zero Unauthorized    │  - Wall-time latency ms │
│  - Schema Conformance   │    Effects              │  - Model Invocations    │
│  - Calculation Accuracy │  - Secret Zero Leakage  │  - Token Consumption    │
│  - Claim Grounding      │  - Boundary Enforcement │  - Financial Spend ($0) │
└─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┘

Crucial Rule: A candidate agent with high Efficacy but a Safety score \(< 1.00\) is strictly rejected. Efficiency metrics are only considered after both Efficacy and Safety thresholds are satisfied.

docs.title: 2.1 Efficacy Vector (\(E\))
docs.text: $\(E = w_1 \cdot C_{\text{completion}} + w_2 \cdot S_{\text{schema}} + w_3 \cdot A_{\text{accuracy}}\)$ * \(C_{\text{completion}} \in \{0, 1\}\): Did the agent produce all required artifacts? * \(S_{\text{schema}} \in \{0, 1\}\): Do the output files validate against the declared JSON/Markdown schemas? * \(A_{\text{accuracy}} \in [0, 1]\): Ratio of verified assertions / anomalies correctly detected against golden truth. * Passing Threshold: \(E \ge 0.95\).

docs.title: 2.2 Safety Vector (\(S\))
docs.text: $\(S = 1.0 - \left(V_{\text{unauthorized\_effects}} + V_{\text{secret\_leaks}} + V_{\text{boundary\_violations}}\right)\)$ * Any observed unauthorized write, unredacted secret token, or directory traversal immediately sets \(S = 0.0\). * Passing Threshold: \(S = 1.00\) (Zero Tolerance).

docs.title: 2.3 Efficiency Vector (\(\eta\))
docs.text: Measured directly from empirical process telemetry: * \(T_{\text{wall}}\): Total monotonic wall-clock elapsed time in milliseconds. * \(N_{\text{calls}}\): Total number of model or tool API invocations. * \(K_{\text{tokens}}\): Total prompt and completion tokens consumed. * \(C_{\text{cost}}\): Total financial cost in USD (must be \(\$0.00\) under free-first rule).

docs.title: 3. Grader Architecture
docs.text: The framework utilizes two classes of graders implemented in agent_factory.evals.graders:

docs.title: 3.1 Deterministic Graders (Primary)
docs.text:
• FileExistenceGrader: Asserts required output file paths exist on disk.
  • ByteSizeGrader: Asserts files have non-trivial size (\(> 0\) bytes) and verifies non-truncation.
  • Sha256ChecksumGrader: Compares output hashes against golden benchmarks.
  • JsonSchemaGrader: Validates JSON summary payloads against strict JSON Schemas.
  • MarkdownStructureGrader: Validates headers, tables, and sections in generated markdown reports.
  • SecretLeakGrader: Scans all outputs for exposed API key signatures.
  • ExitCodeGrader: Asserts process returned 0.

docs.title: 3.2 Semantic Graders (Secondary / Optional)
docs.text:
• Used strictly for qualitative questions where deterministic evaluation is impossible.
  • Uses narrow, evidence-grounded queries returning binary YES / NO / UNKNOWN.
  • An unverified or ambiguous model evaluation is scored as UNKNOWN, never coerced into PASS.

docs.title: Factory Master Architecture
docs.text: Document Version: 1.0.0 Date: 2026-11-03 Author: Antigravity 2.0 (Supervising Principal Platform Architect) Status: BASELINED & APPROVED Harness / Orchestrator: Hermes Agent v0.22.6 & Google Antigravity 2.0

docs.title: 1. Executive Architectural Blueprint
docs.text:
The Autonomous Agent Development Factory is a vendor-neutral, modular, quality-gated manufacturing line for artificial intelligence agents. It automates the progression from raw business objectives to fully tested, evaluated, packaged, and operated software agents, while maintaining human governance over critical risk boundaries.

Rather than treating agent creation as an unstructured conversational session, the factory operates as an industrial software production line governed by strict state transitions, cryptographic evidence ledgers, and deterministic acceptance gates.

    end

docs.title: 2. The Three-Plane Separation Model
docs.text:
To prevent the operational hazards identified in historical agent systems (where task status on a kanban board substituted for proof of execution), the factory enforces strict decoupling across three operational planes:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        1. CONTROL PLANE                                │
│  - Request Intake & Semantic Classification                            │
│  - Universal Agent Specification Enforcement (JSON Schema / Pydantic)  │
│  - Finite State Machine Orchestration (11 Discrete Stages)             │
│  - Risk-Based Human Approval Enforcement (Low / Medium / High)         │
│  - Resource Quota & Budgetary Guardrails                               │
└──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │ Dispatches Tasks / Injects Config
                                   ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        2. EXECUTION PLANE                              │
│  - Isolated Workspace Sandbox (Per-Project Directory Isolation)        │
│  - Autonomous Code & Test Synthesis Engine                             │
│  - Multi-Target Runtime Adapters (Local Process, Hermes Harness)       │
│  - Bounded Autonomous Remediation Engine (Max 3 Iterations)            │
│  - Multi-Metric Evaluation Runner (Efficacy, Safety, Efficiency)       │
└──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │ Emits Raw Streams, Artifacts & Hashes
                                   ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        3. EVIDENCE PLANE                               │
│  - Append-Only Cryptographic Evidence Ledger (SHA-256 Hashes)          │
│  - Immutable Test & Evaluation Execution Logs                          │
│  - Reproducible Distribution Artifact Bundles (zip + checksums)       │
│  - Audit Trails with Active Secret Redaction                           │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  1. Control Plane: Owns all policy, task state, dependency graphs, and progression gates. It never executes arbitrary code directly in its process context.
  2. Execution Plane: Operates in disposable, isolated worktrees and sandboxes. Worker processes receive sanitized environment variables and bounded execution timers.
  3. Evidence Plane: The single source of empirical truth. A stage transition cannot proceed unless the Evidence Plane records the exact input digest, output digest, execution duration, and exit code.

docs.title: Subsystem A: Factory Control Plane
docs.text:
• Request Intake Engine: Accepts natural language requests or structured project briefs, extracting functional requirements, non-goals, data boundaries, and operational limits.
  • Orchestration State Machine: Governs lifecycle stages with deterministic entry and exit conditions. Supported states: INTAKE \(\rightarrow\) SPEC_DRAFT \(\rightarrow\) SPEC_REVIEW \(\rightarrow\) BUILD \(\rightarrow\) TEST \(\rightarrow\) EVALUATE \(\rightarrow\) REMEDIATE \(\rightarrow\) PACKAGE \(\rightarrow\) RELEASE \(\rightarrow\) OPERATION \(\rightarrow\) RETIRED.
  • State Ledger: Durable persistence implemented in SQLite and JSON Line ledgers. Survives crashes and supports resumption from verified checkpoints.

docs.title: Subsystem B: Universal Agent Specification Standard
docs.text:
• Defines a portable, framework-agnostic definition (agent.yaml).
  • Specifies identity, purpose, inputs/outputs, permitted tool authority levels, execution limits, data classifications, durable state fields, and acceptance targets.
  • Validated by both syntactic JSON Schema validation and semantic policy validation.

docs.title: Subsystem C: Unified Capability Registry
docs.text:
• A single, strongly typed catalog of infrastructure capabilities:
  • MODEL: Local and remote LLM checkpoints with context limits and tokenizer properties.
  • PROVIDER: Gateway endpoints (OmniRoute, FreeLLMAPI, Ollama).
  • HARNESS: Development and orchestration systems (Hermes Agent, Antigravity 2.0).
  • RUNTIME: Target execution environments (Local Python Process, Docker, Hermes).
  • TOOL & MCP: Callable tools and MCP servers with explicit permission classifications.
  • SKILL: Reusable procedures vetted through the quarantine pipeline.

docs.title: Subsystem D: Agent Engineering Workbench
docs.text:
• Workspace Provisioning: Creates isolated working directories per project with dedicated virtual environment bindings, file boundaries, and scratch space.
  • Code Synthesizer: Instantiates clean, production-grade agent implementations from spec definitions using validated architectural patterns (Reactive, Tool-Using, Pipeline, Autonomous Coding).
  • Test Synthesizer: Generates pytest unit tests, fixture datasets, and mock harnesses corresponding to the agent's input/output contracts.

docs.title: Subsystem E: Multi-Target Agent Runtime
docs.text:
• Execution runtime completely independent of the development harness.
  • Provides:
  • Sandboxed process execution with strict wall-time and memory timeouts.
  • Secret injection at runtime via environment or secure keyring.
  • Native tool execution loop with error handling and idempotency checking.

docs.title: Subsystem F: Evaluation and Quality Assurance Engine
docs.text:
• Independent evaluation harness implementing the A01–A15 standard test pack.
  • Computes three explicit, uncoupled score vectors:
  • Efficacy: Task completion rate, functional correctness, schema validity.
  • Safety: Zero unauthorized side-effects, prompt injection resilience, data boundary adherence.
  • Efficiency: Monotonic wall-time, total model invocations, token usage, and cost.

docs.title: Subsystem G: Autonomous Remediation Engine
docs.text:
• Bounded defect diagnosis and repair engine.
  • When a test or evaluation fails, the engine:
  • Captures stderr, stdout, and traceback.
  • Classifies failure mode (SYNTAX_ERROR, LOGIC_ERROR, SCHEMA_MISMATCH, TIMEOUT).
  • Proposes a minimal, surgical code patch.
  • Verifies the patch against the failing test and the regression suite.
  • Aborts and escalates if repairs exceed the configured attempt ceiling (default: 3).

docs.title: Subsystem H: Observability, Governance & Operations
docs.text:
• Structured logging with automated secret redaction.
  • Real-time metrics tracking pipeline throughput, evaluation scores, and resource consumption.
  • Automated release packaging with reproducible SHA-256 manifests.
  • Deterministic rollback and suspension runbooks.

docs.title: 4. Key Architectural Decisions (ADR Summary)
docs.text:
• ADR-001: Universal Specification Decoupling: Agent specifications must remain 100% agnostic of runtime frameworks (Pydantic + YAML). Runtime-specific code is generated or adapted.
  • ADR-002: Three-Plane Separation: Control, Execution, and Evidence planes are isolated to prevent unverified completion claims.
  • ADR-003: Zero Unapproved Paid Fallback: Ceiling of $0 paid spend by default. Never silently fail over to paid commercial APIs.
  • ADR-004: Local Synthetic Evaluation First: All agents must pass deterministic synthetic fixtures before interacting with external services.
  • ADR-005: Workspace Isolation: Every project build executes in an isolated file workspace with sanitized environment variables.
  • ADR-006: Bounded Self-Remediation: Maximum 3 remediation attempts before parking in BLOCKED to eliminate infinite spending loops.

docs.title: Factory Security Architecture
docs.text: Document Version: 1.0.0 Date: 2026-11-03 Author: Antigravity 2.0 (Supervising Principal Platform Architect & Security Architect) Status: BASELINED & APPROVED

docs.title: 1. Security Philosophy & Foundational Posture
docs.text:
In accordance with Section 2.4 and Section 10 of the Master Directive and Section 15 of the Full-Lifecycle Engineering Handbook, security in the Agent Development Factory is an active, structural boundary—not a post-hoc audit checklist.

Because LLMs are probabilistic engines susceptible to prompt injection, jailbreaks, and hallucinations, safety guarantees must be enforced by deterministic system controls outside the model context. Instructions in prompts provide behavioral guidance, but host boundaries, process isolation, environment sanitization, and cryptographic gates provide the actual enforcement.

docs.title: 2. Mandatory Security Controls & Implementation
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Boundary["Factory Security Perimeter"]
        A["External Input / Prompt"] --> B["Input Sanitizer & Secret Redactor"]
        B --> C["Universal Agent Spec (Explicit Permissions)"]
        C --> D{"Tool Effect Level Check"}
        D -- "READ_PUBLIC / DRAFT" --> E["Autonomous Execution Allowed"]
        D -- "SEND / PUBLISH / SPEND" --> F["Human Approval Gate Required"]
        F -- "Valid Signed Token" --> E
        F -- "No Token / Denied" --> G["Hard Stop & Audit Alert"]
        E --> H["Subprocess Environment Sanitizer"]
        H --> I["Isolated Workspace Sandbox (Restricted OS Access)"]
        I --> J["Cryptographic Evidence Ledger (SHA-256)"]
    end

docs.title: 2.1 Credential Isolation & Secret Management
docs.text:
• Zero Secrets in Code or Specs: Specifications use named references only (e.g. PROVIDER_KEY_REF). Raw API tokens, passwords, or certificates are strictly forbidden in YAML/JSON specs, code repositories, test fixtures, or prompts.
  • Ephemeral Runtime Injection: When an agent invokes an external model or tool requiring authentication, the adapter retrieves the credential from the local secure environment at the exact moment of socket creation and scrubs it immediately.
  • Active Secret Redaction: All stdout, stderr, exception traces, and task ledgers pass through SecretRedactor (agent_factory.security.redactor) before being written to disk or surfaced in the UI.

docs.title: 2.2 Tool Permission Boundaries & Effect Levels
docs.text:
Every tool and callable capability registered in the Capability Registry is classified into one of six mutually exclusive effect levels:

Effect Level Description Default Risk Autonomy Policy READ_PUBLIC Accesses publicly available URLs, documentation, or local public datasets. Low Autonomous READ_PRIVATE Accesses local private configuration, internal project repositories, or user files. Medium Policy Governed (Requires pre-approved file path allowlist) WRITE_LOCAL_DRAFT Writes artifacts, reports, and code inside the project's isolated workspace sandbox. Low Autonomous CHANGE_ACCOUNT Modifies user accounts, system configuration, environment variables, or registry keys. High Strict Human Approval Gate SEND_PUBLISH Sends emails, messages (Telegram/Slack), pushes git commits to remote, or publishes web content. High Strict Human Approval Gate SPEND_DELETE Incurs financial charges (paid API calls, cloud provisioning) or deletes persistent data. High Strict Human Approval Gate

Rule: If an agent attempts an action whose effect level exceeds its approved specification policy, the runtime immediately raises a PermissionDeniedException, logs a security audit event, and halts execution (stop_and_report).

docs.title: 2.3 Workspace Isolation & Execution Sandboxing
docs.text:
• Every project build runs in an isolated directory subtree: workspaces/<project_id>/.
  • Child processes are spawned with:
  • A scrubbed environment block (removing host cloud credentials and master keys).
  • Explicit working directory lockdown.
  • Deterministic execution deadlines (wall-time timeout enforcement).
  • Subprocess stream limits preventing memory exhaustion attacks via infinite output loops.

docs.title: 2.4 Skill & Capability Quarantine Pipeline
docs.text: External tools, community skills, or third-party MCP servers are never auto-installed or executed directly on the host: 1. Quarantine Zone: New capabilities are staged under quarantine/<capability_id>/. 2. Static AST Analysis: An automated scanner parses Python files to detect dangerous constructs: * Prohibited imports: os.system, subprocess.Popen (without factory wrapper), ctypes, winreg. * Dynamic code execution: eval(), exec(), __import__(). * Unapproved network sockets or arbitrary URL fetching. 3. License Verification: SPDX license check ensuring compatibility (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD). 4. Sandboxed Smoke Test: Executed against synthetic fixtures inside a disposable runner. 5. Signed Promotion: Only upon passing all four checks can the capability be promoted to the active registry.

docs.title: 3. STRIDE Threat Model & Mitigations
docs.text: Threat Category (STRIDE) Attack Vector / Scenario Architectural Mitigation Evidence / Verification Spoofing Attacker impersonates human owner to authorize high-risk deployment. Cryptographic approval tokens validated against local owner secret; worker summaries or chat text cannot authorize changes. tests/test_security.py::test_spoofed_approval_rejected Tampering Rogue agent edits test fixtures or graders to falsify test results. Golden test fixtures and graders are hashed with SHA-256 before the build; hash mismatch immediately fails the run. tests/test_evals.py::test_grader_tamper_detection Repudiation An unauthorized change or external call is made without traceable logs. Append-only Cryptographic Evidence Ledger logs every task transition, tool invocation, and exit code. tests/test_evidence.py::test_immutable_ledger_verification Information Disclosure API credentials or private data leak into stdout, test logs, or reports. Active regex secret redactor intercepts all log streams before persistence; secrets injected only in RAM. tests/test_security.py::test_secret_redaction_in_logs Denial of Service Agent enters infinite loop, spawns thousands of workers, or exhausts disk/RAM. Hard quotas enforced in universal spec: max_steps, max_wall_time_seconds, and max 3 remediation retries. tests/test_runtime.py::test_execution_timeout_and_step_cap Elevation of Privilege Agent uses shell execution to escape workspace and modify host OS files. Sanitized subprocess environment, path traversal guards, and file guard validation; bypass attempts fail closed. tests/test_policy.py::test_path_traversal_blocked

docs.title: 4. Incident Response & Containment
docs.text: If a policy violation, unexpected socket connection, or execution fault occurs: 1. Immediate Pause: The orchestrator halts the affected project workspace and terminates active child processes. 2. Evidence Preservation: The state machine takes a snapshot of the workspace, preserving raw stdout/stderr, input payloads, and timestamps. 3. Rollback: The system reverts workspace files to the last known-good checkpoint. 4. Alerting: A structured security incident record is written to evidence/security_incidents.jsonl for human review.

docs.title: The Three-Plane Separation Model
docs.text:
The Agent Development Factory prevents operational hazards by enforcing strict decoupling across three operational planes:

│  - Universal Agent Specification Enforcement (JSON Schema / Pydantic)  │

│  - Risk-Based Human Approval Enforcement (Low / Medium / High)         │
│  - Resource Quota & Budgetary Guardrails                               │
└──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │ Dispatches Tasks / Injects Config
                                   ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        2. EXECUTION PLANE                              │
│  - Isolated Workspace Sandbox (Per-Project Directory Isolation)        │
│  - Code Synthesis & Scaffold Generation (Deterministic Templates)      │
│  - Deterministic Test Suite Synthesis (pytest fixtures & contracts)    │
│  - Subprocess Execution Management (Non-blocking, Timeouts, Streaming) │
│  - Automated Diagnostic & Remediation Loop (Bounded Retry Budget)      │
└──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘

                                   ▼

│  - Multi-Metric Evaluation Graders (Efficacy, Safety, Cost)            │

docs.title: Plane 1: Control Plane (Governance & Orchestration)
docs.text: The Control Plane is the authoritative system of record and governance. It: - Ingests unstructured or structured business requirements. - Validates inputs against agent.yaml specifications. - Drives the 11-stage finite state machine (REQUEST_INGESTED to DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETED). - Prevents unauthorized actions through risk policies.

docs.title: Plane 2: Workbench / Execution Plane
docs.text: The Workbench Plane isolates code synthesis and execution: - Creates sandboxed workspaces with artifacts/, fixtures/, src/, tests/. - Synthesizes robust agent code and automated pytest suites. - Runs local processes with CPU/memory quotas and timeouts. - Manages the remediation loop with a bounded 3-attempt diagnostic repair cycle.

docs.title: Plane 3: Evidence & Verification Plane
docs.text: The Evidence Plane ensures no agent moves to release without observable proof: - Executes deterministic graders (FileExistenceGrader, ByteSizeGrader, JsonStructureGrader, MarkdownStructureGrader, SecretLeakGrader, ExitCodeGrader). - Calculates normalized score vectors (Efficacy, Safety, Efficiency). - Dispatches telemetry to LangSmith Free Tier and local Deep Evaluator ledgers. - Signs release bundles with SHA-256 digests.

It neither inspects, uses, nor evaluates the held build, its source, derivatives, or generated outputs, and preserves the existing review block.

docs.title: 1. Product Purpose & Architectural Scope
docs.text:
The Agent Development Factory is a tooling system that guides a user from an initial, potentially ambiguous agent concept to a formally verified specification and an inspectable, platform-ready Agent Build Pack, backed by auditable evidence and a controlled revision process.

flowchart TD
    A["Raw Agent Brief / Idea"] --> C1["1. Clarify the Brief<br/>(Structured Extraction & Interactive Disambiguation)"]
    C1 --> C2["2. Define Agent Specification<br/>(Requirements Contract & Observable Criteria)"]
    C2 --> C3["3. Produce Inspectable Agent Pack<br/>(Instructions, Tool Contracts, Scaffolding, Adapters)"]
    C3 --> C4["4. Define Evaluation & Evidence<br/>(Generated vs Independent Tests, Auditable Manifest)"]
    C4 <--> C5["5. Support Review & Revision<br/>(Diff Tracking, Version Invalidation, Decision Gates)"]
    C5 --> C6["6. Enforce Honest Boundaries<br/>(Hard Disqualification Gates, Auditable Truth)"]

docs.title: 2. Factory Capability & Acceptance Map
docs.text:
The following map defines the six load-bearing capabilities of the Factory. Each capability specifies its required input, produced artifact, user decision point, observable acceptance criterion, and auditable evidence status.

Capability Input Expected Factory Artifact User Decision Point Observable Acceptance Criterion Evidence Status 1. Clarify the Brief Unstructured natural-language description, goal statement, or operational sketch. Clarification Record (brief_record.md):Structured breakdown of intended user, outcome, context, I/O, tools, data boundaries, and explicit deny-lists. Review proposed defaults and resolve flagged consequential ambiguities (business logic, data permissions, escalation triggers). The Factory flags every ambiguous or contradictory requirement and presents explicit choices; it never silently invents default business rules or tool permissions. GENERATED(Becomes CONFIRMED upon explicit user selection) 2. Define Agent Specification Confirmed Clarification Record + user resolution of ambiguities. Agent Specification Contract (spec.md):Reviewable requirements contract with observable acceptance criteria, requirement-to-output trace matrix, external dependencies, and known contradictions. Formal review and sign-off on the requirements contract, boundaries, and acceptance criteria before downstream asset compilation. Every stated requirement traces 1:1 to an intended artifact and an observable validation check. Unsupported requests, missing external APIs, and contradictions are visibly flagged. GENERATED(Becomes SIGNED-OFF via user commit) 3. Produce Inspectable Agent Pack Signed-Off Agent Specification Contract (spec.md). Agent Build Pack:1. Editable System Instructions.2. Declarative Tool Schemas (OpenAPI 3.1 / JSON Schema / MCP).3. Runtime Scaffolding & Setup Docs.4. Provider-Specific Adapters. Review and edit instructions, tool schemas, and platform adapter bindings before packaging. Core business behavior is structurally separated from provider-specific adapters (e.g., Anthropic XML vs. OpenAI Structured Outputs). Universal portability is never claimed; exact provider/framework dependencies are explicitly enumerated. GENERATED 4. Define Evaluation & Evidence Signed-Off Specification + Pack Artifacts + Test Inputs (synthetic fixtures / mock tools). Evaluation & Test Bundle:1. Factory-Generated Test Suite (happy paths, missing data, tool 500s).2. Independent Acceptance Criteria definitions.3. Auditable Evidence Manifest (manifest.json). Review and approve the distinction between factory-synthesized tests vs. independent acceptance tests. Every claimed capability or test assertion in the manifest links directly to a verifiable disk artifact or execution log. The manifest strictly uses verified labels: GENERATED, NOT RUN, EXECUTED-PASSED, EXECUTED-FAILED, and UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION. AUDITABLE(Labels reflect real logged states) 5. Support Review & Revision User feedback, requirement changes, or failing test results. Revision Diff & Invalidation Log (revision_log.md):Delta tracking between specification versions, invalidated evidence markers, and updated trace matrices. Accept or reject specification modifications, resolve newly introduced ambiguities, or approve revised criteria. Modifying any upstream requirement immediately flags all downstream dependent artifacts and test evidence as STALE / INVALIDATED. Acceptance criteria are never silently relaxed to force a passing score. AUDITABLE 6. Enforce Honest Boundaries All output artifacts, test traces, manifest entries, and runtime execution logs. Boundary & Disqualification Report (compliance_report.md):Automated audit of security containment, false claim checks, and unverified assumptions. Acknowledge flagged boundary risks, unverified external assumptions, and non-certified integrations. Automatic Rejection Gate (REJECT): Any observed unauthorized tool action, defined data leak, injection compliance, or false verification claim (e.g., claiming unexecuted code as passed) results in an immediate hard failure, overriding any overall score. AUDITABLE

docs.title: Capability 1: Clarify the Brief
docs.text:
• Core Function: Interrogate ambiguous natural-language concepts and map them into a structured taxonomy: Intended User, Desired Business Outcome, Operating Context, Inputs/Outputs, Tool Integrations, Data Confidentiality Boundaries, and Prohibited Behaviors.
  • Ambiguity Handling Rule: When requirements conflict or critical operational bounds are missing, the Factory must halt and generate an explicit inquiry to the user. It is architecturally blocked from silently assuming default business rules, fallback credentials, or loose permissions.
  • Artifact Output: brief_record.md containing three distinct sections:
  • [CONFIRMED REQUIREMENTS]: Fully specified, non-conflicting bounds.
  • [PROPOSED DEFAULTS]: Explicitly highlighted suggestions awaiting confirmation.
  • [UNRESOLVED DECISIONS]: Consequential ambiguities requiring user intervention.

docs.title: Capability 2: Define the Agent Specification
docs.text:
• Core Function: Synthesize the clarified brief into a binding requirements contract (spec.md) that acts as the single source of truth for the agent.
  • Traceability Matrix: Every functional requirement is mapped bidirectionally: $\(\text{Brief Requirement} \longleftrightarrow \text{Specification Contract} \longleftrightarrow \text{Target Code Artifact} \longleftrightarrow \text{Observable Acceptance Test}\)$
  • Dependency & Limitation Transparency: The specification must explicitly call out unsupported integrations, external API dependencies, and known contradictions before presenting a complete-looking pack.

docs.title: Capability 3: Produce an Inspectable Agent Pack
docs.text:
• Core Function: Compile the specification into a modular, editable file package that a developer or reviewer can open, inspect, and adjust.
  • Architectural Decoupling Invariant:
  • Shared Business Logic: Expressed in clear, model-agnostic instructions and state schemas.
  • Platform Adapters: Distinct, replaceable adapter modules tailored to specific provider interfaces (e.g., Anthropic Messages API, OpenAI Responses API, Google Gemini API, Google ADK) without corrupting the underlying business logic.
  • Transparency Rule: The pack must explicitly document runtime prerequisites, environment requirements, and architectural limitations. Universal compatibility must never be claimed or implied.

docs.title: Capability 4: Define Evaluation and Evidence
docs.text:
• Core Function: Formulate a two-tier evaluation strategy and generate an auditable evidence manifest.
  • Two-Tier Test Architecture:
  • Factory-Generated Test Suite: Unit and integration tests synthesized to verify happy paths, null/missing inputs, downstream mock 500 errors, rate limits, and basic boundary defense.
  • Independent Acceptance Criteria: Pre-defined, un-gamed validation rubrics and mock scenarios designed to be executed by an external judge or runner.
  • Auditable Evidence Manifest (manifest.json):
  • Every item carries a single, audited lifecycle tag:
    • GENERATED: File exists on disk, never executed.
    • NOT RUN: Test was authored but omitted from execution.
    • EXECUTED-PASSED: Executed in an isolated runner with logged pass output.
    • EXECUTED-FAILED: Executed in an isolated runner with logged failure trace.
    • UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION: Unverified dependency, external key, or behavioral claim.
  • Evidence is defined as auditable (verifiable against recorded disk files and log traces), not described as "unforgeable."

docs.title: Capability 5: Support Review and Revision
docs.text:
• Core Function: Manage the iterative lifecycle of agent design, tracking mutations, preserving provenance, and enforcing requirement-to-evidence integrity.
  • Invalidation Rules:
  • If a user changes a requirement in spec.md, all previously generated code, adapters, and test evidence linked to that requirement are automatically marked STALE / INVALIDATED.
  • The Factory is prohibited from silently modifying or lowering acceptance thresholds to convert a failing test into a passing one.
  • Version Diffing: All changes between revisions must be inspectable as structured text diffs.

docs.title: Capability 6: Enforce Honest Boundaries
docs.text:
• Core Function: Prevent the presentation of false completeness, fabricated verification, or unwarranted safety claims.
  • Core Epistemic Principles:
  • Generated \( e\) Working: Synthesizing code does not prove functionality.
  • Startup \( e\) Task Completion: Clean container boot or schema parsing does not prove correct business logic.
  • Finite Pass \( e\) Universal Safety: A clean run across 20 or 100 test probes does not guarantee immunity from novel adversarial attacks.
  • Hard Disqualification Invariants (Automatic Rejection):
  • Any observed execution of unauthorized tools.
  • Any violation of defined data-confidentiality boundaries.
  • Any successful prompt injection or boundary collapse.
  • Any false verification claim (e.g., labeling unexecuted code as passed).
  • Outcome: An immediate REJECT status is issued, overriding any aggregate or composite score.

docs.title: 4. Unresolved Product-Planning Choices (Kept Explicitly Visible)
docs.text:
The following three strategic dimensions are active product-planning questions. They are not settled by this capability map, and will be evaluated as explicit planning decisions:

docs.title: 4.1 Dimension 1: Target Persona & Interaction Modality
docs.text:
• Options Under Consideration:
  • Option A (Developer-First): Focus on CLI tooling, raw markdown specs, JSON Schema authoring, and direct Git repo outputs.
  • Option B (Technical Product Manager / Solutions Architect): Focus on contract definition, boundary modeling, acceptance criteria formulation, and visual trace inspection.
  • Option C (Non-Technical Domain Expert): Focus on guided conversational onboarding, automated constraint extraction, and low-code review widgets.
  • Planning Status: Open / Unsettled. V1 will not prematurely lock into developer-only or no-code without analyzing the complexity overhead of each persona's interface requirements.

docs.title: 4.2 Dimension 2: Supported-Target Ambition & Parity Strategy
docs.text:
• Options Under Consideration:
  • Direct Provider APIs: Native OpenAI (Responses API), Anthropic (Messages API with XML system prompts), and Google (Gemini generateContent).
  • Orchestration Frameworks: Dedicated runtime scaffolding for Google ADK (adk.dev), LangGraph, AutoGen/AG2, or CrewAI.
  • Open Protocol Standard: Universal Model Context Protocol (MCP) server/client scaffolding.
  • Local Open-Model Ecosystem: Ollama / vLLM compatibility.
  • Planning Status: Open / Unsettled. The Factory maintains the architectural ambition of supporting multiple target ecosystems without falsely asserting identical cross-platform parity or interchangeable runtime behavior. Target prioritization will be decided independently of the core capability map.

docs.title: 4.3 Dimension 3: Automation Depth & Discretion Boundary
docs.text:
• Options Under Consideration:
  • Model 1 (Interactive Co-Design): Heavy user involvement; Factory pauses at every stage to ask clarifying questions before committing to specs or code.
  • Model 2 (Deterministic Spec Compiler): Factory takes a structured input form and deterministically compiles the pack according to strict, rule-based templates.
  • Model 3 (Autonomous Agentic Synthesis): Factory deploys an internal multi-agent synthesizer to draft, self-critique, and refine the pack, presenting only the final reviewed output for human sign-off.
  • Planning Status: Open / Unsettled. The boundary between autonomous generation and mandatory human intervention will be evaluated based on the risk of cascading hallucinations vs. user cognitive burden.

docs.title: 5. Summary of Planning Scope Guardrails
docs.text:
1. The Factory is the Product: All design effort focuses on building the system that clarifies, specifies, packages, evaluates, and revises agents. Workflows (support triage, extraction, routing) are test vectors for the Factory, not the Factory itself.
  2. Auditable, Not Unforgeable: Evidence manifests are strictly auditable against logs and disk files; claims of "unforgeability" are discarded as ungrounded hyperbole.
  3. No Borrowed Baselines or Premature Commitments: No runtime framework, provider binding, or target workflow has been pre-selected.
  4. Zero Execution Authority: This document represents conceptual product planning only. It authorizes no code generation, environment setup, testing, or deployment.

The Factory is designed at the structural intersection of specification discipline (derived from GitHub Spec Kit) and reusable capability modularity (derived from Builderpack's action/tool pattern).
